z-m-01-07.title: When you add, e always pass wetin dey at start?

z-m-01-07.material: 5 marbles dey inside marble box. Jian talk, 'If you put more marbles inside box, marbles go always pass how many dey there at first!' (Nobody remove marble; dem only add.)

z-m-01-07.s.s1.prompt: Jian talk, 'If you put more marbles inside box, marbles always pass how many dey there at start.' Wetin else you need know before you fit tell whether na true?

z-m-01-07.s.s1.r.c: Whether box big or small, you fit count marbles inside separately. E no concern whether dem go increase.

z-m-01-03.thinking.1: Finding conditions wey make claim hold
z-m-01-03.title: Does changing order give same value?
z-m-01-03.topic: Switching order in addition and subtraction
z-m-01-03.goal: Use new info to narrow when 'switch order gives same value' is right, and find cases where cannot switch.
z-m-01-03.material: Seoyun says about candies, 'When calculate two numbers, switching order gives same value.' Check info piece by piece. Candies can't split/create, or eat more than available.
z-m-01-03.thinking.0: Revise judgment range with new info
z-m-01-03.thinking.2: Check if calculation possible after switching order
z-m-01-03.prereq.0: Experience combine/take-away with numbers up to 10
z-m-01-03.s.s1.prompt: See how thought on claim changes as info arrives.
z-m-01-03.s.s1.hint.0: Find one thing changed in new information.
z-m-01-03.s.s1.hint.1: Say when claim right and when wrong.
z-m-01-03.s.s1.st.0.info: Put together 3 candies and 5 gives 8; 5+3 also 8. Seoyun says order switching always same for two numbers. [3 5 3 5 8 5 3 8]
z-m-01-03.s.s1.st.0.ask: Based on info so far, what think?
z-m-01-03.s.s1.st.0.after: Only combining seen; cautious a/b makes sense. c asserts about unseen cases.
z-m-01-03.s.s1.st.0.o.a: Seems so for combining, but inspect other cases.
z-m-01-03.s.s1.st.0.r.a: This separates observed combining from unseen cases.
z-m-01-03.s.s1.st.0.o.b: Only one example pair, so not sure even about combining.
z-m-01-03.s.s1.st.0.r.b: Careful with few examples; check more.
z-m-01-03.s.s1.st.0.o.c: Believe every two-number calculation works both orders.
z-m-01-03.s.s1.st.0.r.c: You extend combining to all calculations. Haven't seen take-away yet.
z-m-01-03.s.s1.st.1.info: More combining examples: 4+6=10 and 6+4=10; 0+7=7 and 7+0=7. Now eat 4 from 9, leaves 5. Reversed 'eat 9 from 4' impossible, needs unlearned operation.
z-m-01-03.s.s1.st.1.ask: With new info, what think of claim?
z-m-01-03.s.s1.st.1.after: Combining examples keep working; reversed order impossible only for eating. Best judgment separates ranges.
z-m-01-03.s.s1.st.1.o.a: Combining works, but eating can't always switch order.
z-m-01-03.s.s1.st.1.r.a: You separate combining and eating and narrow true range.
z-m-01-03.s.s1.st.1.o.b: Combining or eating, value always same when switch.
z-m-01-03.s.s1.st.1.r.b: Eating case found where switch impossible. Check against example.
z-m-01-03.s.s1.st.1.o.c: Eating example was wrong; can't trust addition case now.
z-m-01-03.s.s1.st.1.r.c: Eating case doesn't undo combining: all three combining pairs still same.
z-m-01-03.s.s1.st.2.info: Let's refine claim. Eating 5 of 5 leaves 0; reversed order also 0. But eating 4 of 9 can't reverse.
z-m-01-03.s.s1.st.2.ask: Choose best revision of Seoyun claim.
z-m-01-03.s.s1.st.2.after: Narrowing range like a, or separating cases like d, properly fixes claim.
z-m-01-03.s.s1.st.2.o.a: When you combine two numbers, switching order gives same value.
z-m-01-03.s.s1.st.2.r.a: This narrows claim to where it is right (combining).
z-m-01-03.s.s1.st.2.o.b: For any two-number calculation, combining or eating, switching always same.
z-m-01-03.s.s1.st.2.r.b: This overextends to all calculations despite eating case where switching impossible.
z-m-01-03.s.s1.st.2.o.c: If write bigger number first, any calculation gives same if switch order.
z-m-01-03.s.s1.st.2.r.c: If bigger first, switched calculation may be impossible. This differs from same-value question.
z-m-01-03.s.s1.st.2.o.d: When you put things together, order no change am, but when you take away, sometimes you no fit switch order.
z-m-01-03.s.s1.st.2.r.d: Dis statement separate putting-together cases from taking-away cases.
z-m-01-03.s.s1.reflect: First information only talk about putting together, so we no know where claim correct. As new information come, you begin separate cases where e correct from where e no correct?
z-m-01-03.s.s2.prompt: For two numbers a and b from 0 to 20, find 2 different cases where you fit both 'take b from a' and 'take a from b.' (If number wey you wan take pass wetin you get, e no fit work.)

z-m-01-03.s.s2.ok.c2: You fit take b from a.
z-m-01-03.s.s2.fail.c2: To take b from a, a no suppose smaller than b.
z-m-01-03.s.s2.ok.c3: You fit also take a from b.
z-m-01-03.s.s2.fail.c3: You no fit take a from b. b smaller than a.
z-m-01-03.s.s2.explain: Na only when number wey you wan take equal wetin you get, both calculations fit work after switching order; then wetin remain na 0. First check whether calculation fit work after you switch order.

z-m-01-08.thinking.1: Find line wey go wrong in solution
z-m-01-08.title: Number wey go in □: how we fit trust am?
z-m-01-08.goal: Learn say you fit check □ values found by different methods with one standard: put your answer back in. Then find one wrong solution and tell friend how to check am.
z-m-01-08.material: For number sentence □+6=14, □ mean 'number wey make 14 when you add 6.' Dohyeon find am by trying numbers in □ one by one, and Sea find am by counting back 6 steps from 14. Gaon solve am another way. ('□+6=14' you read 'box plus six is fourteen.')
z-m-01-08.thinking.0: Checking different methods with same standard
z-m-01-08.thinking.2: Explaining a checking method to friend
z-m-01-08.prereq.0: Experience finding sums for numbers up to 20 and finding number wey make a given total when dem add am
z-m-01-08.s.s1.prompt: For □+6=14, Dohyeon try 7, 9, then 8 inside □ and find 8. Sea count back 6 steps from 14 and find 8. Wetin correct about both methods?
z-m-01-08.s.s1.hint.0: Check whether numbers both of dem find na same.
z-m-01-08.s.s1.hint.1: Put number wey you find, 8, into □, calculate 8+6, see whether e give 14.
z-m-01-08.s.s1.o.a: Na only Dohyeon direct try-number method fit trust
z-m-01-08.s.s1.r.a: This idea trust only direct number-trying method. Sea method also give same number, and you fit check am by putting inside.
z-m-01-08.s.s1.o.b: Na only Sea counting-back method correct
z-m-01-08.s.s1.r.b: This idea accept only counting-back. You also check Dohyeon method by putting number in □.
z-m-01-08.s.s1.o.c: For both methods, you fit check by putting 8 in □

z-m-01-08.s.s1.r.d: Finding am faster no mean say e correct. Standard na whether number you find give 14 when you put am in □.
z-m-01-08.s.s1.explain: Trying numbers and counting back na different ways, but both find same number, 8. Any method you use, you fit trust number if you put am in □ and check say 8+6=14.
z-m-01-08.s.s2.prompt: Gaon find □ in □+6=14 like dis. Choose one line wey hard to believe.
z-m-01-08.s.s2.hint.0: First estimate whether □ likely be number bigger than 14 or smaller than 14.
z-m-01-08.s.s2.hint.1: Read each solution line in order and compare am with your earlier estimate.

z-m-01-04.thinking.0: Find line wey go wrong in solution
z-m-01-04.title: Does '=' always mean say make you write answer?
z-m-01-04.goal: For worked solution, find misunderstanding say '=' only mean sign for writing answer, then judge if number sentences true or false by meaning say both sides get same amount.
z-m-01-04.material: Jiho solve problem to find number for □ in 3+4=□+2. Look at Jiho solution line by line and think wetin '=' dey show. ('3+4' you read 'three plus four', and □ you read 'box.')
z-m-01-04.thinking.2: Calculating each side separately and comparing
z-m-01-04.prereq.0: Experience with simple calculations using numbers up to 10
z-m-01-04.s.s1.prompt: Jiho solve for number in □ in 3+4=□+2 like this. Choose one line wey hard to believe.

z-m-01-04.s.s1.explain: Line 2 na first problem. '=' no always mean say result dey come after am; e mean left side and right side get same amount. If you calculate number sentence on line 3, left side na 7 and right side 7+2 na 9, so dem no equal. So conclusion for line 4 hard to believe too. Wetin you see depend on line wey you choose. Line 1 correct.

z-m-01-04.s.s2.o.a: Na signal to write answer on right side
z-m-01-04.s.s2.r.a: Dis idea see '=' only as place to write answer. E hard to explain number sentences like 7=3+4.
z-m-01-04.s.s2.o.b: Na signal to start calculating left side
z-m-01-04.s.s2.r.b: Dis idea see '=' as command to calculate. E no see say na sign for comparing whether both sides equal.
z-m-01-04.s.s2.o.c: Left side and right side get same amount
z-m-01-04.s.s2.r.c: Dis idea see am as sign say both sides get same amount.
z-m-01-04.s.s2.o.d: Number for left bigger than number for right
z-m-01-04.s.s2.r.d: Dis idea no fit tell 'same' from 'bigger'. 'Bigger' get another sign.

z-m-01-05.goal: Compare closeness by number of steps on number line, learn cases where you no fit say which one nearer, then make numbers wey fit conditions by yourself.
z-m-01-05.material: Imagine 40, 41, 42, ..., 60 dey line up one step apart on number line. We compare how near two numbers be by how many steps between dem on number line. Fewer steps mean nearer. This time, think only about natural numbers.

z-m-01-05.thinking.1: Learning about cases where you no fit decide
z-m-01-05.thinking.2: Making plenty numbers wey fit conditions

z-m-01-05.s.s1.explain: From 47 to 50 na 3 steps, and to 40 na 7 steps. Side wey get fewer steps dey nearer.
